interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins (0.0), no seminal vesicle invasion (0.0), absence of lymph node metastasis (0.0), and absence of lymphovascular invasion (0.0). The preoperative PSA was elevated at 12. The surgical pathology showed a Gleason 4+5 with tertiary pattern 3 (ISUP grade group 5) and pathological T3a with extraprostatic extension. Countervailing factors include the high preoperative PSA and the high pathological grade/stage. The biopsy grade (Gleason 0+0, ISUP grade group 0) differed significantly from the prostatectomy specimen (Gleason 4+5, ISUP grade group 5). Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data significantly widens the uncertainty regarding the trajectory. The current heuristic horizon suggests a time frame of approximately 87 months to recurrence. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and its subsequent trajectory would be crucial in refining this prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 87.17 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 69.73–104.60 months; its coverage has not been validated.
